docs.summary: Shared plumbing for the built in decoders. Header parsing lives in [`ParseHeader`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Decoders.DecoderBase~ParseHeader); pixel decoding is opt in through [`CanDecodePixels`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Decoders.DecoderBase~CanDecodePixels) so a decoder can ship identification support before its codec is written.
Extensions conventionally used for this format, leading dot included, lowercase. Purely informational; detection is driven by content.

Whether pixel decoding is implemented. When false the decoder still reports header facts through [`TryIdentify`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Decoders.DecoderBase~TryIdentify) and [`TryDecode`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.Decoders.DecoderBase~TryDecode) fails with [`NotImplemented`](#api~Prowl.Aperture.ApertureError~NotImplemented).

docs.summary: Reads the container header. Implementations must treat every field as hostile: bounds check before indexing, reject impossible geometry, and never loop on a value the file controls without a hard cap.

docs.summary: Decodes the image, honouring the limits and conversions in `options`.

Whether the pixels this decoder returns are still in the order the file stored them, so a recorded orientation is work outstanding rather than a fact already dealt with. A format that turns its own rows the right way round, as Radiance and the bitmap both do, says no and reports its orientation as a description of the file.
Lifts whatever ancillary blocks the container carries. The default finds none, which is the right answer for a format that has nowhere to put them.

docs.summary: Picks the smallest lossless pixel layout that can hold the described samples. Alpha can arrive from outside the channel count, as a PNG transparency chunk does, so it is passed separately and promotes the result to a layout that has somewhere to put it.
